name: divider
title: Divider
description: A rule marking a change of topic within a page, or a separation between groups in a toolbar.

base.summary: One hairline in the divider colour `theme.border.default` documents. No margin: the stack it sits in owns the space either side.

tokens.margin: space.0 — the parent's gap places it, as with Heading
tokens.inline-size: the full width of its container

vertical.summary: The same hairline on the other axis, stretching to the height of the row it divides.

tokens.block-size: stretched to the row by the parent's alignment

behavior.summary: An `<hr>` when horizontal, a `role="separator"` element when vertical, or an `aria-hidden` rule when `decorative`. No primitive: a non-focusable separator has no interaction to own.

decisions.decision: Most lines in a UI are not Dividers
decisions.why: The rule between table rows is the table's, the rule between menu groups is `MenuSeparator`, the rule between a stack of Disclosures belongs to the stack, and the outline of a Card is the card's. Each of those is a border owned by the component that knows where it goes. A Divider is for the one case none of them cover: a change of topic in running content, or a group boundary in a row of controls. If you are placing a Divider between every item of a list, the list should own the border.

decisions.decision: Semantic by default, `decorative` to opt out
decisions.why: An `<hr>` is a thematic break, announced as a separator, and it tells a screen-reader user what a sighted reader sees: the topic changed here. When the line is only visual — the gap would have done, but the design wants a line — `decorative` hides it so a reader does not hear "separator" between two things that are not separate. Defaulting the other way would make every semantic break silent unless the caller remembered.

An `<hr>` is horizontal by definition, and styling one vertical leaves it announcing the wrong orientation. A vertical divider between toolbar groups is a `div` with `role="separator"` and `aria-orientation="vertical"`, which is what the ARIA toolbar pattern expects.

"— or —" between two sign-in options is a sentence, not a rule, and rendering text inside a separator makes a screen reader either skip the text or read the separator as content. Write the word as text between two decorative dividers if the design needs it. A labelled divider is not part of this gate.

Web: `<hr>` horizontally; `<div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical">` vertically; with `decorative`, the same element with `aria-hidden="true"` (and `role="none"` on the `<hr>`). React Native has no separator role: a hairline `View` that is always hidden from assistive tech with `importantForAccessibility="no"` and `accessibilityElementsHidden`, whatever `decorative` says — the topic change is carried by the heading that follows it, which is the only structure native screen readers navigate by. `decorative` therefore has an effect on web only. Rata-drawn (decision N5): there is no OS separator control. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

use: `vertical` between groups of controls in a horizontal row, such as a toolbar.
dont: `vertical` between two columns of a page layout. That is the layout's border, not a separator.

decorative.summary: Hides the rule from assistive tech when it marks no real change of topic.
use: A line the design wants where the content does not change subject — around an "or" between two sign-in options.
dont: Every divider, by habit. A real topic break should be heard as one.
decorative.a11y: Adds `aria-hidden="true"`. Web only: on React Native the rule is always hidden.

use: The space the page wants either side, which this component deliberately does not own.
dont: A thicker or coloured rule. A heavier boundary is `theme.border.strong` on the component that owns it, not a restyled divider.

usage.case: A change of topic in running content
usage.when: Two parts of a page about different things, where a heading alone would be too quiet.
usage.example:
<Text>Your plan renews on 1 March.</Text>
<Divider />
<Heading level={2}>Danger zone</Heading>
usage.notes: Semantic, so it is announced as a separator. The space either side comes from the parent's stack gap, not from the divider.

usage.when: A row of controls in two or more groups.
usage.notes: Vertical renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, which is what the toolbar pattern expects between groups.

usage.when: A rule between every row of a list.
usage.notes: Don't. A screen reader hears "separator" between every row, and the list cannot drop the last one cleanly. The list owns its row borders — a Table, or the list's own CSS with `theme.border.default`.
